title: A locally finitely presented universal single-direct-image rank representative
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be flat, proper and locally of finite presentation, and let $E,F$ be finite locally free modules [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module] on $X$. There are a scheme $W$ and an immersion $j:W\to S$ locally of finite presentation such that every $g:T\to S$ factors through $j$ if and only if $\mathrm{PicardUniversalSingleRankMatch}(f,E,F,g)$ [def-sc-picard-universal-single-rank-match]. There is no structure-sheaf unit or connected-fibre assumption; only the ordinary direct image of $F$ is tested.

source.place: Tags 0BDP (first three proof paragraphs), 0B91 and 0BDL; the homogeneous-fibre and empty-fibre decomposition is the adaptation explicitly given in the parent node lem-sc-picard-universal-rank-match-locus-lfp-core.

proof.text: Choose standard derived category models. The single-rank predicate is preserved by precomposition: apply its universal quantifier to the composite and reassociate the three morphisms.
Use the existing theorem that the single-rank predicate is source local.

At each point obtain an unrestricted perfect chart, covering homogeneous, empty and mixed fibres. Apply the lowest-cohomology locus theorem in degree zero at the chart rank. Compose its representing equivalence with the inverse chart comparison to give a local immersion representing the single-rank predicate, retaining local finite presentation.

Apply the locally finitely presented immersion gluing theorem to this predicate and its local representatives. This gives the asserted global immersion, local finite presentation and full factorization criterion.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_picardUniversalSingleRankLocus_finitePresentation
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [Flat f] [IsProper f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f]
    (E F : X.Modules) [E.IsFiniteLocallyFree] [F.IsFiniteLocallyFree] :
    ∃ (W : Scheme.{u}) (j : W ⟶ S),
      IsImmersion j ∧ LocallyOfFinitePresentation j ∧
      ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S),
        (∃ h : T ⟶ W, h ≫ j = g) ↔ PicardUniversalSingleRankMatch f E F g
